# STD-TEC-MKD-001: Formatting

**Standards Metadata**

```yaml
standard_id: 'STD-TEC-MKD-001'
standard_name: 'Markdown Formatting'
standard_type: 'technology'
category: 'technology'
version: '1.0.0'
status: 'active'

tags: ['technology', 'markdown', 'formatting', 'mandatory']
```

---

> Defines the formatting standards for Markdown documents within enterprise environments. Ensures consistency, readability, and maintainability across all documentation, including proper document structure, formatting guidelines, content organization, and style conventions.

---
page_texts.3:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#purpose]

## Purpose

This standard establishes requirements for creating and formatting Markdown documentation within enterprise environments to ensure consistency, readability, and maintainability across all technical documentation.
page_texts.4:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#20-document-structure]

## 2.0 Document Structure

All Markdown documents in enterprise environments should follow a consistent structure that includes the following components.
page_texts.5:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#21-document-title]

### 2.1 Document Title

Every document should begin with a clear, descriptive level-1 heading (`#`) that serves as the document title:

```markdown
# Document Title
```

The title should be concise and accurately reflect the document's content.
page_texts.6:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#22-breadcrumb-navigation]

### 2.2 Breadcrumb Navigation

Following the title, include breadcrumb navigation that allows users to easily navigate back to parent sections:

```markdown
Back to [Project](../../../README.md) | [Architecture](../../README.md) | [Application](../README.md) | [Standards](./README.md)

---
```

The breadcrumb navigation should include all parent categories in the document hierarchy, providing a clear path back to higher-level documentation.
page_texts.7:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#23-document-change-log]

### 2.3 Document Change Log

Include a change log table to track document versions, authors, and changes. README.md files in the root of a folder may not include a change log if the file is simply an index of other files in the folder. The change log should be formatted as follows:

```markdown
## Document Change Log

| Version | Author      | Description            | Date       |
| ------- | ----------- | ---------------------- | ---------- |
| 1.0     | Author Name | Initial document       | YYYY-MM-DD |
| 1.1     | Author Name | Description of changes | YYYY-MM-DD |
```

or
page_texts.8:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#document-change-log-with-status]

## Document Change Log with Status

| Version | Author      | Description      | Date       | Status     |
| ------- | ----------- | ---------------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| 1.0     | Author Name | Initial document | YYYY-MM-DD | `Proposed` |
page_texts.9:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#24-table-of-contents]

### 2.4 Table of Contents

A table of contents with links to all major sections and subsections helps readers navigate longer documents:

```markdown
## Table of Contents

-   [1.0 Overview](#10-overview)
-   [2.0 Section Name](#20-section-name)
    -   [2.1 Subsection Name](#21-subsection-name)
    -   [2.2 Subsection Name](#22-subsection-name)
```

Links should use lowercase headings with hyphens replacing spaces and special characters removed.
page_texts.10:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#25-content-sections]

### 2.5 Content Sections

The document body should be organized into numbered sections with a clear hierarchy. Each major section should begin with a brief introduction.
page_texts.11:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#26-related-standards]

### 2.6 Related Standards

End the document with links to related standards or other relevant documentation:

```markdown
## 7.0 Related Standards

-   [API Design Standards](../../application/api/STD-APP-API-001-api-design.md)
-   Documentation Style Guide _(Coming Soon: `./documentation-style-guide.md`)_
```
page_texts.13:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#31-section-numbering]

### 3.1 Section Numbering

Use the following numbering scheme for document sections:

- Major sections: `1.0`, `2.0`, `3.0`, etc.
- Subsections: `1.1`, `1.2`, `2.1`, etc.
- Sub-subsections: `1.1.1`, `1.1.2`, etc.

This numbering should be reflected in both the table of contents and the section headings.
page_texts.14:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#32-heading-hierarchy]

### 3.2 Heading Hierarchy

Use heading levels consistently throughout the document:

- Level 1 (`#`): Document title only
- Level 2 (`##`): Major sections (e.g., `## 1.0 Overview`)
- Level 3 (`###`): Subsections (e.g., `### 1.1 Purpose`)
- Level 4 (`####`): Sub-subsections when necessary
- Avoid using heading levels 5 and 6 if possible
- Always include a blank line after any heading line (with #, ##, ###, etc.) to prevent formatting errors

Example of correct heading formatting:

```markdown
## Section Title

This is the section content. The blank line above this paragraph is required for proper rendering.

### Subsection Title

This is the subsection content. The blank line above this paragraph is also required.
```
page_texts.15:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#33-lists-and-tables]

### 3.3 Lists and Tables

- Use bullet points (`-`) for unordered lists
- Use numbers (`1.`, `2.`, etc.) for ordered lists or sequences
- Format tables with proper headers and alignment:

```markdown
| Header 1 | Header 2 | Header 3 |
| -------- | -------- | -------- |
| Cell 1   | Cell 2   | Cell 3   |
| Cell 4   | Cell 5   | Cell 6   |
```
page_texts.16:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#34-code-blocks]

### 3.4 Code Blocks

When creating code blocks, follow these guidelines:

- Always include a blank line before code block delimiters (```) to prevent formatting errors
- Always specify the language for syntax highlighting
- Use proper indentation in code examples

```markdown
This is some text.

​`typescript
function example(param: string): boolean {
  return param.length > 0;
}
​`
```

For configuration files or plain text, use appropriate language identifiers (`json`, `yaml`, `bash`, etc.) or `text` if no specific highlighting is needed.
page_texts.17:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#35-links-and-references]

### 3.5 Links and References

- Use relative links for internal documentation: `[Link Text](relative/path/to/file.md)`
- Use absolute links for external resources: `[Link Text](https://example.com)`
- For section references within the same document, use: `[Section Name](#section-name)`
page_texts.18:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#36-images]

### 3.6 Images

When including images:

- Store images in a `.assets` folder within the same directory hierarchy as the markdown file
- Use relative paths to reference images
- Include descriptive alt text
- Specify dimensions if needed

```markdown
![Alt text for image](.assets/diagram.png 'Optional title')
```
page_texts.19:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#361-image-storage-convention]

#### 3.6.1 Image Storage Convention

The `.assets` folder convention ensures that:

- Images are stored close to the documentation that references them
- Images are clearly separated from code and documentation files
- The dot-prefix ensures the folder is treated as a hidden resource in most file browsers
- Each documentation section maintains its own assets, improving organization

Example directory structure:

```text
documentation/
├── README.md
├── .assets/
│   ├── architecture-overview.png
│   └── component-diagram.png
├── component-a/
│   ├── README.md
│   └── .assets/
│       └── component-a-diagram.png
└── component-b/
    ├── README.md
    └── .assets/
        └── component-b-diagram.png
```
page_texts.20:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#362-mermaid-diagrams]

#### 3.6.2 Mermaid Diagrams

Mermaid is a JavaScript-based diagramming tool that renders text definitions into diagrams directly within Markdown. Use Mermaid for simple diagrams that benefit from being maintained directly in the markdown file:

````markdown
```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Start] --> B{Decision}
    B -->|Yes| C[Process 1]
    B -->|No| D[Process 2]
    C --> E[End]
    D --> E
```
````

Common Mermaid diagram types:

- Flow charts (`graph` or `flowchart`)
- Sequence diagrams (`sequenceDiagram`)
- Class diagrams (`classDiagram`)
- State diagrams (`stateDiagram-v2`)
- Entity relationship diagrams (`erDiagram`)
- Gantt charts (`gantt`)

Use Mermaid when:

- The diagram is relatively simple
- The diagram benefits from being updated along with the text
- Version control of the diagram as text is important
page_texts.21:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#363-drawio-diagrams]

#### 3.6.3 Draw.io Diagrams

For more complex diagrams, use Draw.io (also known as diagrams.net):

1. Create diagrams using the Draw.io desktop application or web interface
2. Export the diagram as a `.drawio.png` file, which combines both the diagram image and the editable Draw.io source
3. Store the diagram file in the `.assets` folder
4. Reference the image in your Markdown as shown in the image example below

Example of storing and referencing Draw.io diagrams:

```text
documentation/
├── architecture.md
└── .assets/
    └── system-diagram.drawio.png  # Combined image and source file
```

In your Markdown:

```markdown
![System Architecture Diagram](.assets/system-diagram.drawio.png)
```

Use Draw.io when:

- Creating complex diagrams with detailed visual elements
- Precise control over diagram layout is required
- Collaboration on diagram design is needed

The `.drawio.png` format offers several advantages:

- Single file that serves as both image and source
- Can be viewed in any image viewer or browser
- Can be edited directly in Draw.io by opening the PNG file
- Eliminates the need to maintain separate image and source files
- Ensures diagram source is always available with the image
page_texts.23:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#41-writing-style]

### 4.1 Writing Style

- Use clear, concise language
- Write in the present tense
- Use active voice when possible
- Keep paragraphs focused on single topics
- Use consistent terminology throughout documentation
page_texts.24:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#42-technical-terminology]

### 4.2 Technical Terminology

- Define technical terms on first use
- Be consistent with capitalization of product names and technical terms
- Reference the project dictionary for standard terminology
page_texts.25:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#43-examples-and-illustrations]

### 4.3 Examples and Illustrations

- Include practical examples to illustrate complex concepts
- Provide code snippets that can be copied and used directly
- Use diagrams when they help explain complex relationships or workflows
page_texts.27:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#51-naming-conventions]

### 5.1 Naming Conventions

- Use kebab-case for all Markdown file names (e.g., `markdown-formatting-standards.md`)
- Choose descriptive file names that reflect the content
- Avoid using spaces or special characters in file names
- For standards documents, use the pattern: `topic-name-standards.md`
- For decision records, use the pattern: `adr-NNN-descriptive-name.md`
page_texts.28:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#52-file-organization]

### 5.2 File Organization

- Organize files in logical directories according to the repository structure
- Place related documents in the same directory
- Use README.md files to provide directory-level guidance
- Maintain consistent structure across similar document types
page_texts.30:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#61-markdown-editors]

### 6.1 Markdown Editors

Recommended Markdown editors and tools:

- Visual Studio Code with the following extensions:
    - Markdown All in One
    - markdownlint
    - GitHub Markdown Preview
- GitLab/GitHub built-in Markdown editors for quick edits
page_texts.31:
[standards/technology/markdown/STD-TEC-MKD-001-formatting.md#62-pre-commit-validation]

### 6.2 Pre-commit Validation

- Use markdownlint to validate Markdown syntax before committing
- Configure CI/CD pipelines to check Markdown formatting
- Review documentation changes as part of the pull request process
